specName: The ADP Plug-in for Visual Studio Code
intent: etalii.adp.ide.vscode produces one installable VS Code extension with the Gartner hype cycle graph and Agent Behavior Modelling diagrams, conforming to their definitions here, with tests, one-step debugging and a pipeline that offers the plug-in for download
context: area: etalii.adp.ide.vscode (plug-in, tests, debug setup, .github/workflows/build.yml, readme, docs/tools.md)
reference: etalii.adp.ide.intellij spec 005-continuous-integration and its naming
reference: etalii.adp.ide.standalone src/diagrams/gartner-hype-cycle-graph and agent-behavior-modelling, pull requests 120 and 122
constraint: constitution principle I, a host implements the definition rather than its own variant
expectations: versioned releases, signing and marketplace publishing
any tool other than the two diagrams
changes to the standalone or IntelliJ hosts
a DISL runtime as a deliverable of its own

decisions.decision: Downloads are the plug-in from each run and a Development build pre-release; versioned releases and marketplaces follow in their own specification
decisions.why: the ask is an artifact to download, and IntelliJ spec 005 is the model

decisions.decision: Markdown stays in the text editor by default; a behavior model is opened by choice, and .ghg opens in the diagram by default
decisions.why: .md is a shared extension in the definition

decisions.decision: Arrange diagram is in scope and both definitions are updated for it in this repository first
decisions.why: standalone has it since pull request 122 and the definitions do not state it yet

decisions.decision: Driving the tools from their .dis files or implementing them by hand is left to the plan (FR-008)
decisions.why: it is a how; FR-006 holds either way

decisions.decision: Plan and tasks approved without review at Peter's instruction (2026-10-05): auto approve and start implementing
decisions.why: he wants implementation to proceed overnight

decisions.decision: Hand-written TypeScript in three layers (core, extension, webview); custom text editors; SVG canvas without a UI framework; toolbox in the editor, properties as a view
